source.episode_title: The First Gospel in the Curse
source.anchor_kjv: And the LORD God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
source.thread: Grace, spoken into a sentence, before the Judge ever turns to the guilty
source.hook_line: Dust on their skin, fig leaves tied with shaking hands — Adam and Eve stand in the trees, waiting to hear what God will do to them.
source.spoken_script: Dust on their skin, fig leaves tied with shaking hands — Adam and Eve stand in the trees, waiting to hear what God will do to them. But before God ever tells them their sentence, He turns to the snake first and buries a promise for them inside that curse. To the serpent God says, "And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel." Only then does He turn to Eve, then Adam, to speak their own sentence. Call it a curse formula — the order still stands: rescue spoken before ruin. It's easy to admire a God who promises rescue. It's harder to believe He meant it for you — before you'd done one thing to earn it, or even asked. That promise has a name now: Jesus, the Seed who crushed the serpent's head. Grace was spoken before your sentence — come meet the Voice that spoke first.

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE
- title_candidates[2] 'Before God Spoke to Adam, He Spoke to the Snake' is false: Genesis 3:9-13 has God questioning Adam and Eve BEFORE the serpent's curse. Drop it. The chosen title is accurate only in the narrow sense that the curse on the serpent (with the promise) precedes the sentences on Eve and Adam; keep the description's wording 'before He speaks their sentence'.
- youtube_short: 'waiting to hear what God will do' is narration framing, not text. Acceptable.
- Verse quote verbatim KJV: PASS.
